what: Stage 3 analysis freeze of the survival measurement-validity study (plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-29-survival-measurement-validity-study.md, D-117; design reports/survival_measurement/stage2_design.md, D-119). Populations, transforms, definitions, clustering and decision rules, fixed BEFORE any Stage 2 output exists. Thresholds are the plan's proposed ones, accepted by the user's Q33 answer (a) of 2026-10-29; everything the plan left open is fixed here and recorded in D-120.
written: 2026-10-29 06:10 IST (first draft; revised 06:15 IST after the read-only review of session project-fe), before Stage 2 ran: no Ada job exists and no sidecar sums exist
status: DRAFT until the read-only review of session project-fe; committed (with analysis_freeze.sha256) before any Stage 2 output is read. After the commit it is never edited: a deviation is written into the report as a deviation.

inputs.sums: the saved sidecar files sums_INT16/INT6/INT4.pt of job sc-legacy, sums_INT6/INT4.pt of sc-matched and of sc-gptq (reports/survival_measurement/stage2/README.md): 21 float64/int64 statistics per (language, feature) on the equal-budget stream (D-015), mask regime, 27 languages x 16,384 features; n per language in the same files
inputs.meta: each job's meta.json (theta, gate results) and scripts/g0/survival_validate.py must report ok for the job; a job that failed a gate is not analysed
inputs.committed: survival.pt of the arm's stage-1 run mask/eq (check_committed): used for G2(ii) only
inputs.h5: the F5 inputs and the 1,487-feature sample of scripts/g0/survival_effect.py (load_arm, feature_table, reliable_mask; D-113), unchanged
inputs.selectivity: selectivity.pt of the legacy mask/eq run (FP tagging; identical for every arm), key `selective`

population.active: FP-ACTIVE cell = (language, feature) with FP firing rate n_a / n > 0.001 (Duan's rule, as Stage 1) AND n_a >= 20 (redundant on the full run: the equal budget is 27,036 tokens per language, so a rate above 0.001 already means n_a >= 28; kept for subset runs). The FP-active set depends on the full-precision model only: it is the SAME set in every condition and arm. The population is defined PER QUANTITY and never conditions on the quantized side except where the quantity needs it: nu, the flip rates, the margin, H3's nu half and ALL of H4 use every FP-active cell with NO condition on b (a feature that goes completely silent after quantization stays in, with its large perturbation). lambda, r (H3's lambda half) use every FP-active cell with Stage 1's clip convention (survival_lambda.lam: r <= 0.001 or undefined counts as clipped low, r above 1 - 1e-6 as clipped high; counted, never dropped). Only the decomposition statistics g and sigma_e (log|g|, log sigma_e^2) need g != 0 and sigma_e^2 > 0; cells without them are excluded from those descriptive tables only and counted.
population.reference_width: INT16 (legacy arm; identical in every arm by construction)
population.silent_cells_reported: for every (arm, width): the number and share of FP-active cells that are silent after quantization (n_b == 0), overall and per tier and per language, and the number of clipped lambda cells (low, high)

definitions.moments: from the saved sums with n = tokens of the language: mean_a = Sa/n, var_a = Saa/n - mean_a^2, likewise b; cov = Sab/n - mean_a mean_b (population moments; the same sums as the committed Pearson formula)
definitions.sigma_a: sqrt(var_a): the full-precision spread of the feature in that language (the quantity in lambda's denominator); log FP scale = log sigma_a
definitions.r: the LangPearson formula (denominator clamp 1e-12, result clamp [-1, 1]); lambda = survival_lambda.lam(r) (clip convention of Stage 1, clipped cells counted)
definitions.gain: g = cov / var_a; offset c = mean_b - g mean_a; sigma_e^2 = var_b - g^2 var_a (residual variance); co-active versions from the *_both sums
definitions.lambda_identity: lambda = log sigma_e^2 - 2 log|g| - 2 log sigma_a (g != 0, sigma_e^2 > 0); sigma_a is the same in every arm, so a cross-arm difference of lambda is exactly (difference of log sigma_e^2) - 2 (difference of log|g|)
definitions.nu: nu_j = sqrt(S_dpre2 / n_a) / theta_j (RMS over FP-active tokens of the encoder pre-activation change, in threshold units); log nu with nu floored at 1e-12
definitions.flips: on_off = n_on_off / n_a; off_on = n_off_on / (n - n_a); exact flip share = n_exceed1 / n_a (equals on_off, gate G4); predicted flip share = n_exceed2 / n_a
definitions.margin: mean margin = S_d / n_a / theta_j (in threshold units)

gates.identity: r recomputed from g, sigma_a, sigma_e (r = g sigma_a / sqrt(g^2 sigma_a^2 + sigma_e^2), sign of g) equals r from the sums within 1e-4 for every FP-active cell with sigma_e^2 > 0 whose r from the sums is not clamped (|r| < 1 and denominator above the 1e-12 clamp). Cells with sigma_e^2 <= 0 (cancellation when r is near 1), a clamped r, or sigma_b = 0 are EXCLUDED from the check and counted per condition (treated as clipped high / clipped low for lambda, as in Stage 1). A correctness gate, not a finding; failure of the 1e-4 rule on the remaining cells stops the analysis.
gates.validated_jobs: scripts/g0/survival_validate.py ok for the three jobs (sacct, log, checksums, meta gates G1-G4 and G6, sums, weights manifest against the recorded hashes)
gates.G2_committed: reported by check_committed. If it passed in all arms, the report may say the sidecar sees the same weights and tokens as stage 1. If it failed anywhere, every Stage 3 number is labelled 'sidecar-internal' and the 'same as stage 1' statement is not made; the identity gate and H3-H5 are still evaluated on the sidecar's own sums

bootstrap.interval: percentile 95 % unless a rule below says 90 %
bootstrap.note: H5 uses scripts/g0/survival_effect.py's own N_BOOT and SEED unchanged

H3.statistic: per language, over its FP-active cells: Spearman(lambda, log sigma_a) (clip convention of Stage 1, clipped cells included at their clipped lambda) and Spearman(nu, log sigma_a) (no condition on b); the median over the 27 languages per (arm, width)
H3.rule: met for a cell (arm, width in INT6, INT4) if |median Spearman(nu, log sigma_a)| < 0.2 AND |median Spearman(lambda, log sigma_a)| > 0.5 (the plan's proposed thresholds). H3 as a whole is 'met' only if it is met in all six cells (3 arms x INT6, INT4); otherwise the report lists which cells fail. INT16 (legacy) is reported, not part of the rule.
H3.sensitivity: the same with log max activation as the scale (the Stage 1 proxy); reported, not part of the rule

H4.outcome: per language y_l = MINUS the mean of log nu over ALL its FP-active cells (no condition on b; higher = less perturbation, the direction of Stage 1's tier test); tier score and script-family dummies as in Stage 1 (phase1_analysis.TIER_SCORE low 0, mid 1, high 2; partial_slope)
H4.estimands: per width w (INT16 legacy, INT6 and INT4 of each arm): slope_w = partial_slope(y_w, tier, script); the standardized slope z_w = slope_w * SD_l(tier score) / SD_l(y_w), SD over the 27 languages, each width with ITS OWN SD(y_w) (a partial-correlation-like scale comparable across widths; the INT16 spread of log nu may be dominated by arithmetic noise and is not used as a common denominator). PRIMARY (INT16-referenced, the quantization-specific part): s_w = z_w - z_INT16. SECONDARY, same wording and bound: z_w itself against 0 (plan H4 as written: does the perturbation differ by tier after scale is removed). SENSITIVITY: s_w' = (slope_w - slope_INT16) * SD(tier) / SD(y_INT16) (the common INT16 denominator). Also reported with the sigma_a covariate (log10 of the language's median sigma_a over its FP-active cells) in the reduced model.
H4.intervals: cluster bootstrap over languages (2,000 replicates); z_w, z_INT16 and s_w recomputed on the same resample (including SD(y) and SD(tier) of the resample); 95 % interval for 'differs / present', 90 % interval (two one-sided tests at 5 %) for 'equivalent / absent'. Replicates in which the script-residualised tier has zero variance or SD(y) is zero are dropped and their number reported; if more than 5 % of the replicates are dropped for a cell, its interval is 'not estimable' and its outcome 'inconclusive'.
H4.equivalence_bound: 0.20 in s_w (a small standardized effect of the quantization-specific tier difference), fixed here before any value
H4.rule: per (arm, width in INT6, INT4), for the PRIMARY s_w and, with the same wording, for the SECONDARY z_w: 'present' (a quantization-specific tier difference, resp. a tier pattern in the perturbation) if the 95 % interval excludes 0 AND |estimate| >= 0.20; 'absent' ONLY if the 90 % interval lies inside (-0.20, +0.20); otherwise 'inconclusive'. A non-significant p-value is never read as 'no effect'. 'Inconclusive' is an acceptable and reportable result: with four single-language script families absorbed by the dummies (Han, Japanese, Hangul, Ethiopic) the tier slope rests on about 23 effective languages, so a 90 % interval inside +-0.20 is demanding; the bound is NOT widened after seeing data. The tier slope and z at INT16 are reported as the reference (a tier pattern that exists with a near-zero weight change is a property of the measurement).
H4.selectivity_secondary: descriptive only, no rule: per language the difference of mean log nu between selective and non-selective FP-active cells (selective = the committed `selective` mask), languages with at least 20 selective FP-active cells; mean over languages with a 95 % cluster interval, per (arm, width)

H5.statement: g and nu added to model B (D-113) do not reach the 10 % target for W1: expected null, reported to bound the claim
H5.design: scripts/g0/survival_effect.py unchanged: models A and B as in D-113 per (arm, state in INT6, INT4); model B+ = base columns + R1 + gain g + log nu, where g and nu are the sidecar values of the feature's own (language, feature) cell at that state (per-(feature, state) covariates from different tokens than R1 and W1); the same quantile transform, ridge grid, leave-language-out folds, reliability mask and cluster bootstrap
H5.population: F5 features with n_a >= 20 in the sidecar; A, B and B+ are all evaluated on this population (the D-113 full-population value is reported next to it)
H5.rule: the D-113 rule unchanged: improvement of B+ over B in mean absolute error >= 10 % relative AND the cluster-bootstrap interval of the improvement above zero (survival_effect.improvement, cell_met). Also reported: B+ over A, and g-only and nu-only variants. Overall statement as survival_effect.overall_statement

descriptive: lambda decomposition by arm and width: median g, median log sigma_e^2, median lambda, cross-arm differences of the two components (exact identity above)
flip rates (on_off, off_on) by arm and width, median and 10th/90th percentile over cells
nu distribution by arm and width (median, quartiles) and by tier
Spearman between predicted and exact flip share over cells
counts of dropped cells per condition and reason
Deming/OLS slope of log nu between arms (the metric-2 analogue of Stage 1's H1)

outputs.generator: scripts/g0/survival_stage3.py (written test first after this freeze is committed; imports survival_lambda, survival_effect, phase1_analysis, survival_sidecar; refuses to run if analysis_freeze.json does not match analysis_freeze.sha256 or if a job is not validated)
outputs.tests: tests_torch/test_survival_stage3.py with a toy sums set whose answers are known, and a mutation battery

limits: one model, one layer, one SAE, simulated weight-only quantizers, 27 languages (clusters)
lambda as 'noise' assumes the residual is unrelated to a; flips and nu are measured directly for that reason
post hoc relative to Stage 1 (same tokens and features were seen as correlations); Stage 3 rules are fixed before the new statistics exist
H4 is about 27 languages and one tier coding; equivalence is claimed only inside the stated bound

four script families hold a single language (Han, Japanese, Hangul, Ethiopic): the script dummies absorb those four languages, so the H4 tier slope effectively rests on about 23 languages; an 'inconclusive' H4 outcome is expected to be common and is a result, not a failure
the FP-active set is fixed by the full-precision model, so a feature silenced by quantization stays in the analysis (it is the damaged end of the distribution, not a missing value)
revision: Review of session project-fe, 2026-10-29: (1) populations per quantity, no condition on b for nu, flips, margin, H3's nu half and H4 (selection bias: silent features); (2) identity gate excludes degenerate cells (sigma_e^2 <= 0 or a clamped r) and counts them; (3) H4 standardizes each width by its own SD of y (the INT16-SD version is a sensitivity); (4) slope_w against 0 is also reported under the same wording; (5) single-language script families and degenerate bootstrap replicates stated and handled; (6) 'inconclusive' is stated to be an acceptable result; minor: n_a >= 20 is redundant on the full run and kept for subset runs.
